tasks.short: Research historic places and materials for conservation

steps.what: Define historical research questions for the place or material
Locate archive records, plans and historical references
Examine original sources and historic places or materials
Record provenance, dates and evidence for identification or reconstruction
Interpret historical evidence and write conservation implications
Send checked historical findings to conservation colleagues

tasks.design: Configure archive-reference capture and a provenance record in {DOCS}. The historian examines evidence and writes the conservation interpretation personally, then checks the final research packet before its separate {EMAIL} handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Archive identifiers and provenance details are repeatedly located and copied into working records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference fields and linked research-note headings can reduce repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing original fabric, later changes and uncertain reconstructions from incomplete evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Critical comparison of documentary and physical evidence.
tasks.altitude: More traceable research supporting conservation decisions.

reach.task: Use historical evidence in place decisions

evidence.claim: Native reference capture and provenance templates can plausibly reduce repeated record work; no historic-conservation time case is supplied by this digest.

assumptions: Includes research, the actual evidence record, written implications and internal handoff; physical conservation or reconstruction is downstream work.

Historian produces scope in s1, archive identifier and location in s2, observations in s3, and date, attribution, quotation or image reference, rights and uncertainty in s4. All capture is counted. Missing metadata and ambiguous dates are researched and recorded manually.
Try native catalogue links and note fields first; no model infers missing history or authorises conservation work.
Ordinary author saves remain fully retained inside the writing steps with no self-approval.
unknowns: Whether the handoff is internal or to an outside client
research_questions: Can source capture reduce entry without merging conflicting dates or attributions?

incremental.description: Maintain reference fields and archive links

approvals.approved_version: Exact findings packet, uncertainty notes, source attachments and internal recipients; changes require renewed final-version check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R89 gross11 less2 upkeep gives central9. Low retains19/20 source search and19/20 provenance entry because records lack stable identifiers: gross2 less2=0. High retains17/20 search and16/20 entry with compatible archive references and a useful research-note layout: gross7 less2=5. Scope, original examination, interpretation and real handoff stay full.

tasks.short: Present historical accounts through individuals and social groupings

steps.what: Assemble checked historical sources and presentation requirements
Choose historical framing and explain grouping limitations
Write historical accounts from the chosen interpretation

loop.purpose: Express the historian's account for the chosen audience
loop.input: outline, interpretive points and supplied source passages
loop.check: Historian checks attribution, historical context, uncertainty and represented groups
loop.stop: One revision then manual rewrite if context or source fidelity fails
loop.why_not_simpler: Historical explanation requires varied prose around the selected evidence

steps.what: Check historical account for accuracy and fair representation
Format account headings, captions and source references
Present final historical account to its audience

tasks.design: Use native source links and presentation styles in {DOCS}; a bounded loop drafts prose from the historian's own outline. Formatting is an explicit machine action, followed by a human check of the final account before public presentation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence, narrative prose and layout are assembled repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting and native layouts can reduce mechanical preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Historical framing, contested identities and avoiding anachronism or unsupported generalisations.
tasks.human_edge: Interpretation sensitive to evidence, people and audience.
tasks.altitude: Clearer accounts with traceable interpretive choices.

reach.learn: Make grouping choices and limitations visible

evidence.claim: The digest reports a public report with apparent AI-generated errors and fabricated references; source checking remains necessary in historical accounts.
Native formatting and bounded narrative drafting have unmeasured local timing.

assumptions: Includes account writing, formatting and actual presentation; source research for the underlying project is counted once where performed.

The historian captures source identifier, passage, date, attribution, rights and layout fields in s1, and produces chosen framing in s2. Their capture time is counted. Missing provenance or incompatible caption fields require manual completion before formatting.
Native styles and source fields come first; the loop cannot invent biographical facts or choose social categories.
The author saves internally without a separate approval; the final public version is checked at the presentation action.
research_questions: Can drafting preserve attribution and uncertainty while reducing account preparation time?

incremental.description: Maintain layouts and examine draft errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact formatted narrative, captions, source references and audience context; changes in text or images require renewed final-version check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R78 gross22 less3 upkeep gives central19. Low retains14/15 source assembly,33/35 drafting and4/5 formatting with unfamiliar groupings and incomplete captions: gross4 less3=1. High retains13/15 assembly,26/35 drafting and1/5 formatting with a reusable layout and well-supported explanatory passages: gross15 less3=12. Framing, final historical review and presentation stay full.

tasks.short: Research a country, region or historical period

steps.what: Define country, region or period research questions
Search catalogues and locate relevant historical sources
Read sources and compare their historical contexts
Record quotations, chronology and source qualifications
Interpret historical patterns and write provisional conclusions

tasks.design: Configure saved catalogue searches and source-linked research notes in {DOCS}. The historian reads originals, evaluates context and writes the provisional interpretation; native fields support references and quotations rather than supplying historical conclusions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Researchers repeatedly locate source records and enter the same bibliographic details into notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference import and note headings can reduce handling where archive metadata are usable.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete evidence, conflicting accounts, language and interpretation of period-specific meanings.
tasks.human_edge: Critical judgement grounded in the original sources.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated source administration and a more traceable research trail.

reach.learn: Keep source perspective separate from the event described

evidence.claim: The digest identifies ASReview for prioritising literature records; that capability does not replace historical reading or establish a saving for archival research.
Saved catalogue searches and native reference notes may reduce handling; these estimates are E1.

assumptions: Includes research notes and written provisional conclusions. Publication and presentation are separately priced when undertaken, not implied by this research-only task.

Historian produces geographic and temporal scope in s1, source title, archive identifier, date and access location in s2, observations in s3, and quotation, page or folio, attribution and uncertainty in s4. All capture is counted; missing or incompatible archive metadata are entered manually.
Native saved searches and citation fields come first; no automatic interpretation, fabricated transcript or invented date.
Normal same-system saves have fully retained negligible time and no extra approval gate.
unknowns: Archive metadata availability and language coverage
Existing reference import and search configuration
research_questions: Does reference reuse reduce note handling without losing page, folio or attribution context?

already_counted.description: Check source results and research notes

incremental.description: Maintain search terms and repair reference mappings

tasks.short: Research history and publish findings and theories

steps.what: Form historical research questions and publication argument
Find historical evidence and capture publication source details
Examine sources and develop historical findings and theories
Write source notes and record theory qualifications
Write publication text explaining findings and theories

loop.purpose: Draft the historian's selected argument with traceable evidence
loop.input: argument notes, quotations and source identifiers
loop.check: Historian checks chronology, attribution, causal claims and uncertainty
loop.stop: One revision then manual rewrite if evidence or argument is distorted
loop.why_not_simpler: Interpretive exposition needs varied prose beyond a fixed article layout

steps.what: Check and revise final historical publication
Submit final historical findings and theories for publication

tasks.design: Use native reference and article structures in {DOCS}, with a bounded draft from the historian's own argument notes. Research, source-note writing, publication writing, final revision and the external {EMAIL} submission are explicit steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference handling and explanatory writing are repeated across research publications.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference reuse and source-bound drafting can reduce assembly without choosing a historical theory.
tasks.still_hard: Original interpretation and justified claims from incomplete or conflicting evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Scholarly judgement and accountability for the published account.
tasks.altitude: More attention to defensible historical arguments and evidence gaps.

reach.learn: Separate evidence, inference and alternative accounts

evidence.claim: The digest reports fabricated references in a public report, supporting retained citation checks rather than unreviewed publication.
Reference reuse and bounded publication drafting savings are E1 scenarios.

assumptions: This is an end-to-end publication project, retaining its research and notes. If the same episode also satisfies tasks3720 or3725, allocate its baseline and saving once rather than adding all task scenarios together.

Historian produces research scope in s1, source identifier, date, location and permissions in s2, findings in s3, and passages, page or folio, uncertainties and argument notes in s4. Capture remains counted; unresolvable citations and missing evidence are handled manually and cannot enter the submitted text as fact.
Native reference fields and article headings come first; no synthetic historical evidence or automatic theory selection.
Normal author saves are fully retained and ungated; only actual publication submission has a final-version gate.
unknowns: Extent of overlap with other research task statements
research_questions: Can historians retain equivalent source fidelity with less time writing the explanatory draft?

incremental.description: Maintain source layouts and monitor drafting errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact final publication, references, illustrations, destination and submission message; any change requires renewed final-version check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R83.5 gross16.5 less3 upkeep gives central13.5. Low retains19/20 retrieval,9/10 notes and19/20 publication writing with unfamiliar sources and mostly original prose: gross3 less3=0. High retains17/20 retrieval,8/10 notes and14/20 writing with compatible source metadata and reusable exposition: gross11 less3=8. Research judgement, source examination, final revision and actual submission remain full.

role.altitude: Reduce repeated source and prose assembly while retaining original historical inquiry and interpretation.
role.ambitious_version: A historian who can show the evidence behind each account and devote more time to difficult sources and interpretations.
